White student enrollment at General Ray Davis Middle falls to 87 for 2024-25
D. S. Dunn
In the 2024-25 school year, General Ray Davis Middle School registered 87 white students—a 12.1% decline compared to the prior year—citing figures from the Georgia Department of Education.
The school’s total enrollment numbered 875 students this year. White students accounted for 10% of the student population, ranking as the third-largest demographic group.
General Ray Davis Middle School is part of Rockdale County School District, headquartered in Conyers.
Out of 18 schools in the Rockdale County School District, Heritage High School had the largest number of white students enrolled for 2024-25, totaling 138.
Based on data from the National Center for Education Statistics, public school enrollment across Georgia included approximately 36.4% Black students, 35.9% white, 18.1% Hispanic, 4% Asian, 4.6% multiracial, 0.2% American Indian or Alaska Native, and 0.1% Pacific Islander.
Chronic absenteeism continues to challenge Georgia schools following the pandemic, with 20.7% of students missing at least 10% of school days in 2024, according to the Georgia Department of Education. The GaDOE initiated efforts statewide, including launching a real-time attendance dashboard, running a public awareness campaign, and providing targeted assistance for districts with heightened needs to raise daily attendance rates.
For 2025, Georgia legislators approved changes to school attendance laws, prohibiting expulsion solely on the basis of absenteeism. The bill also introduces enhanced reporting obligations and coordinates with programs offering alternative diploma pathways.
By 2026, Georgia’s average student-to-teacher ratio stood at close to 14:1, outperforming the nationwide average of 15:1.
